title: Programmable functional RNA design with a virtual scientist - Nature Biotechnology
text:
AbstractProgrammable functional RNA design is central to synthetic biology and therapeutics, yet both human expertise and existing computational methods struggle to directly program the three-dimensional structures that govern function. Here we introduce RhoAgent, an agentic system that designs RNA candidates and iteratively refines them using experimental feedback. RhoAgent uses RDiff, a diffusion-based generative tool conditioned on base interactions and functional motifs. First, we validate RhoAgent by generating diverse and active ribozymes with only 40–70% sequence similarity to their wild-type counterparts. Second, we enhance the cleavage efficiency of the structurally uncharacterized hovlinc ribozyme by up to sixfold relative to the human-expert-truncated construct. Furthermore, RhoAgent generates a fluorogenic aptamer scaffold that improves fluorescence by 230% relative to the wild-type aptamer. Finally, we design three-dimensional scaffolds that spatially position two distinct functional cores, creating aptamer-based Förster resonance energy transfer systems. This design overcomes a key barrier in compositional RNA design by preserving the binding activities of both components.

Data availability

The training dataset comprises experimentally determined RNA structures from the PDB (https://www.rcsb.org/), supplemented with sequences from the bpRNA database (https://bprna.cgrb.oregonstate.edu/) and the Ribonanza dataset (https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/stanford-ribonanza-rna-folding/data). All PDB structures used in this study are publicly available. Designed RNA sequences are provided in Supplementary Tables 2–20. Source data are provided with this paper.
Code availability

RhoAgent and RDiff are available via GitHub at https://github.com/ml4bio/RhoAgent and https://github.com/ml4bio/RDiff and via Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22879438 (ref. 65). In addition, we used the software with the indicated version numbers in this study: cmbuild, cmcalibrate, cmscan and cmsearch from Infernal 1.1.3; cd-hit-est from CD-HIT 4.8.1; nhmmer from HMMER 3.3; HH-suite 2.0.15; Python = 3.8.12; NumPy = 1.21.2, a Python package for numerical calculations; PyTorch = 1.10.2, a deep learning framework in Python; pandas = 2.3.1, an open-source Python package for data analysis; r-base = 4.5.2; r-ggplot2 = 4.0.1, a system in R for declaratively creating graphics; SciPy = 1.14.1, an open-source Python package for mathematics; RNApolis is a Python library and utilities containing RNA-related bioinformatics functions and classes, available via GitHub at https://github.com/tzok/rnapolis-py; and Arena, a standalone program used for the full-atomic reconstruction of RNA structures from coarse-grained models, available via GitHub at https://github.com/pylelab/Arena.
